citation: Biswas et al., Learning by Teaching: A New Agent Paradigm for Educational Software
intervention: Betty's Brain teachable agent with self-regulation support
comparator: tutored and baseline LbT variants
main_evidence: self-regulation support better prepared students for later learning
limitation: pre-LLM concept-map interaction
relevance: foundational teachable-agent architecture

citation: Chase et al., Teachable Agents and the Protege Effect
intervention: students believed they taught a teachable agent
comparator: students believed they learned for themselves
main_evidence: teaching framing increased effort and time on learning activities
limitation: children and non-conversational agent
relevance: theoretical motivation for responsibility framing

citation: Kobayashi, Learning by Preparing-to-Teach and Teaching: A Meta-Analysis
intervention: teaching after preparing to teach
comparator: studying without teaching expectancy
main_evidence: Hedges g 0.35 for preparing and 0.56 for preparing plus teaching
limitation: not specific to LLM teachable agents
relevance: supports interactive teaching and deep-learning outcomes

citation: Debbane et al., Learning by Teaching: Key Challenges and Design Implications
intervention: teaching another person and teaching alone
comparator: comparison across teaching configurations
main_evidence: psychological and teaching know-how barriers affected LbT
limitation: not an efficacy experiment; virtual agents rated hypothetically
relevance: requires scaffolding and credible feedback

citation: Jin et al., Teach AI How to Code
intervention: TeachYou with Reflect-Respond, mode-shifting, and Teaching Helper
comparator: same Reflect-Respond and seed knowledge state without mode-shifting or Teaching Helper
main_evidence: problem-solving knowledge-building density: 8.4 +/- 7.1% versus 3.5 +/- 6.6%; p=0.03; Cohen d=0.71
limitation: two components changed together; no direct pre/post learning gain; algorithm and procedural-knowledge scope
relevance: closest baseline and motivates isolating active questioning from other support

citation: Chen et al., Learning by teaching with ChatGPT
intervention: GPT-4 teachable agent after videos
comparator: videos plus individual coding
main_evidence: higher adjusted knowledge score and clearer code; no significant correctness difference
limitation: small sample and agent could generate correct code
relevance: motivates measuring correctness separately from explanation quality

citation: Love et al., Teaching a Conversational Agent using Natural Language
intervention: typed paraphrases to teach agent
comparator: sentence selection from source
main_evidence: paraphrasing felt more helpful but did not improve actual gain in a fixed interaction
limitation: non-LLM context and fixed-duration interaction
relevance: perceived benefit must not substitute for learning outcome

citation: Arun et al., Chrysalis
intervention: learning by teaching an LLM
comparator: being tutored by an LLM
main_evidence: LbT messages were longer; no quiz-score difference and ceiling effect
limitation: advanced students; preprint; tutor versus tutee rather than active versus passive tutee
relevance: supports within-subject design and warns about quiz ceiling

citation: Xing et al., Development of a generative AI-powered teachable agent
population: 320 middle school students and 6 teachers across three studies
design: design-based research with usability testing and three iterations
intervention: ALTER-Math generative AI teachable agent
comparator: design iterations rather than one fixed efficacy comparator
main_evidence: documents iterative classroom design of a generative teachable agent
limitation: math and design-based evidence do not identify the isolated effect of questioning
relevance: shows that classroom deployment needs iterative usability work

citation: Roscoe and Chi, Understanding Tutor Learning
intervention: learning through explaining and questioning
comparator: knowledge-building versus knowledge-telling behaviors
main_evidence: knowledge-building explanations and reflective questioning are proposed mechanisms of tutor learning
limitation: review predates LLM agents and does not estimate one intervention effect
relevance: foundation for transcript coding and the primary outcome

citation: Matsuda et al., Tutor Learning Using a Teachable Agent That Asks for Explanations
intervention: SimStudent asks the student tutor for explanations
comparator: teachable-agent condition without self-explanation prompts
main_evidence: explanation prompts produced comparable learning with fewer practice problems in the same time
limitation: short conference paper and pre-LLM rule-based agent
relevance: direct precedent for agent-initiated why and how prompts

citation: Okita and Schwartz, Learning by Teaching Human Pupils and Teachable Agents
population: students teaching a human pupil or teachable agent
intervention: tutors observed the pupil or agent apply what had been taught
comparator: direct feedback without observing the tutee's subsequent performance
main_evidence: recursive feedback improved transfer more than direct feedback alone
limitation: non-LLM domain and feedback manipulation differs from question policy
relevance: motivates showing whether the AI actually learned from the explanation

citation: Jaeger et al., Agency Concepts and Use of Teachable-Agent Technology
intervention: students taught and queried a teachable agent
comparator: differences in learners' prior concepts of human and machine agency
main_evidence: agency concepts predicted learning behavior and changed through interaction
limitation: correlational components and a non-conversational pre-LLM agent
relevance: supports measuring perceived agency and controlling persona credibility

citation: Lee et al., Curiosity Notebook
population: 12 elementary students and 41 university students across two studies
design: four-week field study plus online observational study
intervention: web platform for teaching a conversational agent
comparator: two design iterations rather than an efficacy control
main_evidence: demonstrates a reusable platform for observing learning-by-teaching interactions
limitation: platform and design evidence rather than causal learning evidence
relevance: informs transcript capture lesson resources and controlled agent state

citation: Lachner et al., Learning-by-Teaching Without Audience Presence or Interaction
intervention: preparing instructional explanations with or without an audience
comparator: interactive and non-interactive learning-by-teaching settings
main_evidence: separates retrieval organization elaboration and social-presence mechanisms
limitation: explicitly not a review of teachable-agent efficacy
relevance: clarifies which mechanisms require an interactive AI learner

citation: Ma et al., How to Teach Programming in the AI Era
intervention: HypoCompass LLM teachable agent for debugging hypotheses
comparator: pre-test versus post-test without a control group
main_evidence: debugging score increased 11.7 percent and completion time decreased 13.6 percent
limitation: small selected sample and no causal comparator; item difficulty may confound subskills
relevance: closest programming example beyond AlgoBo and a warning against overclaiming pre-post gains

citation: Rogers et al., Playing Dumb to Get Smart
intervention: LLM-based teachable agent embedded in university courses
comparator: evaluation conditions reported in the full paper
main_evidence: establishes feasibility of deploying an LLM tutee in authentic CS classes
limitation: full outcome extraction still required before using quantitative claims
relevance: high-priority replication context for university CS deployment

citation: Liu et al., Engagement Patterns with AI Teachable Agents
intervention: AI teachable agent with natural-language questions and follow-ups
comparator: improved group n=327 versus declined group n=206
main_evidence: constructive interaction was more common in the improved group while passive activity was more common in the declined group
limitation: observational grouping does not establish that interaction patterns caused improvement
relevance: motivates coding interaction quality rather than relying on turn count

citation: Shahriar et al., Beyond Prior Knowledge: The Predictive Role of Knowledge-Building in Tutor Learning
intervention: SimStudent in APLUS with GPT-3.5 ExpectAdapt adaptive follow-up questions
comparator: no control condition; variation in tutors' knowledge-building response ratio
main_evidence: %KBR positively predicted conceptual and procedural post-test scores after prior knowledge was included in the model
limitation: small sample; one condition; path associations do not establish a causal effect of follow-up questions
relevance: supports knowledge-building ratio as a process outcome but requires a randomized question-policy test

citation: Ceha et al., Can a Humorous Conversational Agent Enhance Learning
intervention: teachable conversational agent using affiliative self-defeating or neutral humor
comparator: three humor styles
main_evidence: affiliative humor increased motivation and effort but learning effects were not uniformly improved
limitation: persona manipulation may change social experience without changing learning
relevance: warns that persona and tone must remain fixed across active and passive conditions
